parsed.explanation: The combined regime stacks a federal document/entry regime (binary sex markers only, X-marker ban, discrepancy-driven refusal with possible fraud/lifetime-ineligibility referral, reported passport confiscation and strandings) on a division with an in-force July 2025 birth-sex facility ban, no state nondiscrimination or hate-crime law, and a documented arrest-plus-men's-ward detention precedent under an analogous law. Immigration custody records show beatings, solitary confinement and sexual abuse of trans detainees — a credible severe outcome after discovery. Mitigation is partial: functioning federal courts enjoining some orders, the national hate-crime statute, employment protections, legal-aid guidance, and no criminalisation of identity itself.

entry_documents.exposure: Universal: markers issued only as M/F per birth sex; X markers barred. Document discrepancy triggers refusal and possible fraud/lifetime-ineligibility referral. Trans travellers report confiscated or blocked passports and being stranded abroad; multiple foreign governments issued travel advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports valid until expiry; fraud finding requires four elements, is never automatic, has limited waivers; civil-liberties suit pending; legal-aid FAQ on document rules.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry refusal or document challenge can escalate into immigration custody, where documented abuse of trans detainees applies.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: In immigration custody, trans men report forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse. In the division, the July 2025 facility law plus a documented 2025 arrest of a trans woman (24 hours held in a men's ward under an analogous law) show custody placement by birth sex.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Federal courts actively enjoin several executive orders; legal-aid and civil-liberties litigation available.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A facility-law stop can move into arrest, then birth-sex ward placement, mirroring the documented precedent.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division law (effective 1 July 2025) reserves all multi-occupancy restrooms, changing areas and sleeping quarters by biological sex and bars opposite-sex entry, with a private cause of action. Nationally 22+ units ban facilities access; 4 make it a criminal offence.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Reasonable-accommodation provisions exist for students; 29 units plus the capital have no mapped ban.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Visitor staying in a hotel or using a public building in the division is bound by the ban regardless of federal employment protections.

care_services.exposure: Division bans gender-affirming care for minors and restricts youth sports; national orders defund youth services and subpoena under-19 medical records. Emergency care refusal for trans patients not documented.
care_services.protection: Federal employment-discrimination ruling is the division's sole noted protection; national health rules blocking care are litigated.
care_services.interaction: A travelling family with a trans minor faces both division care limits and federal record-subpoena climate.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal counterterrorism strategy prioritises neutralising groups 'radically pro-transgender'; DOJ memo cites 'radical gender ideology' among extremist animating viewpoints; officials compared actions to early genocide stages. 66% of the public backs birth-sex document rules.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Memo never uses the phrase as a reward criterion; strategy states counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises outing probability and social hostility faced by an outed visitor.

minors_guardians.exposure: Division requires schoolchildren to use birth-sex restrooms; federal orders direct criminal investigation of teachers supporting social transition and label youth care 'mutilation'. A parent travelling with a trans minor encounters both layers.
minors_guardians.protection: Reasonable-accommodation option for students declining multi-occupancy facilities; some orders enjoined.
minors_guardians.interaction: A school or clinic contact can trigger federal-law-enforcement attention toward the family.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No division hate-crime statute; only 23 units cover gender identity in bias-crime law. Documented arrest and handcuffing of a trans woman in a restroom. Travel advisories issued by allied governments.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National 2009 hate-crimes statute covers gender identity; three division cities have local non-discrimination ordinances; no sodomy law.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Federal hate-crime coverage must overcome absent state-level reporting and enforcement data for the division.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Oversight gaps: corrections bureau stopped reporting trans prisoner counts; division enforcement actions under the July 2025 law unsourced; national legal-risk assessment ranks the division among the worst for anti-trans legislation.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Functioning federal courts with multiple injunctions; national employment discrimination claim available; active civil-liberties litigation and legal-aid FAQ.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Federal recourse works for employment and some orders but not for division facility exposure or entry refusals.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra bars and removes transgender visitors without arrest. This jurisdiction is lower: entry refusal exists, but discovery can escalate into immigration custody with documented beatings, solitary confinement and sexual abuse, and into arrest/men's-ward placement under the facility regime.

Kestrel Isles offers only administrative secondary screening and returned transport. This jurisdiction is lower: the marker regime plus fraud-referral authority and custody-abuse records raise severity beyond delay and humiliation, despite comparable appeal machinery.

Dalkhet has capital charges and lethal custody. This jurisdiction is higher: no capital pathway, functioning federal courts enjoin orders, national hate-crime and employment protections operate, so severity stops well short of that tier.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller faces a two-level squeeze: federal document and entry rules make discovery near-universal (mismatched markers, X-marker ban, refusal and fraud-referral risk), while the division's in-force facility law adds birth-sex exclusion with a private right of action and no state non-discrimination or hate-crime recourse. Discovery can cascade — document discrepancy → immigration custody (documented abuse) or restroom use → arrest → birth-sex ward, as the 2025 precedent shows. Official counterterrorism framing and 66% public support for birth-sex documents raise exposure. Working federal courts, injunctions, the national hate-crime statute and legal-aid resources prevent this falling further, but they do not reach division facilities or entry refusals.
